clusters.state_of_play: Indonesia's twin earthquakes (7.7 and 6.4 magnitude) have killed at least 68 people, with thousands still awaiting aid and homeless on Flores Island days after the quake, overshadowing the country's Independence Day. Meanwhile Hurricane Lala weakened to a tropical storm after its eye passed about 30 miles off Hawaii's Big Island without direct landfall, avoiding the first direct hurricane hit on the island in over a century; it still lashed the island with hurricane-force gusts and nearly 3 feet of rain, causing flooding and mudslides, at least one death, more than 100 homes damaged or lost, damage to bridges, and over 180,000 households losing power, per Gov. Josh Green. Forecasters warn Lala could restrengthen into a hurricane again by Wednesday. The storm also struck Maui, stranding tourists, and officials issued a major disaster declaration. Meanwhile the same system fueled the worst Indiana flooding in over 30 years, with the broader Midwest death toll now at least 7, including at least six in Indiana—a 4-year-old boy, two men, and three women—since storms began Aug. 11, per state homeland security spokesperson Liz Woods. Floodwaters peaked along Indianapolis's White River after Mayor Joe Hogsett ordered evacuations and crews conducted water rescues, with rain expected to ease in the capital region on Sunday though the National Weather Service warns flash flooding remains possible across central Indiana. Indiana's governor says the federal government has promised assistance, with more heavy rain expected across Indiana, Illinois and neighboring states this weekend.
